learning_outcomes.text: System Engineering will be able to explain its relationship with all other engineering disciplines in the natural sciences and its scope and field of work independently of them.
The system will be able to easily distinguish between subsystems and lower-level components. It will have sufficient knowledge about the processes followed in their designs.
The students will be able to participate in and contribute to work related to determining, managing, and verifying the correct requirements in system/device design.
Understand and be able to apply the importance of product lifecycle, configuration management, and change process implementation.
The students will learn the importance of auditing, decision-making, risk, and opportunity concepts in design and production processes.
The students will have the knowledge and practical skills to ensure the integration and harmonization of work between different engineering disciplines.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Systems Engineering; System Definition and Systems Engineering.
Definition of General Life Cycle; Definition of Life Cycle, Characteristics, and Stages
Definition of General Life Cycle; Life Cycle Approaches
Technical Processes and Procedures; Job and Task Analysis, Identification of Stakeholder Needs and Requirements
Technical Processes and Procedures; Defining system requirements, Creating system architecture
Technical Processes and Procedures; System Architecture Design and Design Definition Processes
Technical Processes and Procedures; Implementation, Integration, and Verification Processes
Technical Processes and Procedures; Operation, Maintenance, and Decommissioning/Disposal
Technical Management Processes and Procedures; Project Planning, Process Monitoring and Control, Decision Making, Risk Management, Configuration Management
Technical Management Processes and Procedures; Configuration Management, Information Management, Measurement and Quality Assurance
Cross-cutting Systems Engineering Methods, Model-Based Systems Engineering, Prototyping, Interface Definition, AGILE Systems Engineering
Special Engineering Activities; Safety Engineering, Electromagnetic Compatibility, Environmental Conditions and Impact Analysis, Logistics Engineering, Production and Manufacturability Analysis
System Engineering approaches in Automotive, System Engineering in Hardware and Software
Current topics and developments in Systems Engineering.
